label: Glossary

label: Glossary
text: A number of the form a + bi, where a and b are real numbers and i = √(−1).

label: Glossary
text: Conjugate

label: Glossary
text: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi.

label: Glossary
text: General form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = ax² + bx + c. Shows opening, axis of symmetry and y-intercept.

label: Glossary
text: Vertex form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = a(x − h)² + k. Shows vertex (h, k) and axis of symmetry x = h.

label: Glossary
text: Intercept form (quadratic)

label: Glossary
text: y = a(x − α)(x − β). Shows x-intercepts α and β.

label: Glossary
text: Axis of symmetry

label: Glossary
text: A vertical line that passes through the vertex of the parabola and lies exactly midway between the two x-intercepts (if they exist). Equation: x = −b/(2a).

label: Glossary
text: Centroid (G)

label: Glossary
text: The point where the three medians of a triangle meet. Always lies inside the triangle. Coordinates: ((x_a + x_b + x_c)/3, (y_a + y_b + y_c)/3). AG : GD = 2 : 1.

label: Glossary
text: Orthocenter (H)

label: Glossary
text: The point where the three altitudes of a triangle meet. Inside for acute, at the right-angle vertex for right-angled, outside for obtuse.

label: Glossary
text: Circumcenter (O)

label: Glossary
text: The center of the circumscribed circle, formed by the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors. OA = OB = OC (radii).

label: Glossary
text: Incenter (I)

label: Glossary
text: The center of the inscribed circle, formed by the intersection of the angle bisectors. DI = EI = FI (radii). pr = 2A. Coordinates: ((ax_a + bx_b + cx_c)/(a + b + c), (ay_a + by_b + cy_c)/(a + b + c)).

label: Glossary
text: Euler's line

label: Glossary
text: For all triangles, the circumcenter O, the centroid V and the orthocenter H lie on the same line.

text: If PQ is a perpendicular bisector of BC, then any points on PQ can form isosceles sides with BC (e.g. PB = PC and OB = OC).

label: Glossary
text: Angle Bisector Property

label: Glossary
text: If BI is an angle bisector of ABC with AB ⊥ DI and BC ⊥ IF, then DI = IF.

text: (a) Prove, by mathematical induction, that for all positive integers \(n\),

label: Mathematical Induction
text: \(1 \times 2 \times 3 + 2 \times 3 \times 4 + 3 \times 4 \times 5 + \ldots + n(n+1)(n+2) = \dfrac{n(n+1)(n+2)(n+3)}{4}\).

label: Mathematical Induction
text: (b) Using (a) and the formula \(1 \times 2 + 2 \times 3 + 3 \times 4 + \ldots + n(n+1) = \dfrac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{3}\), prove that \(1^2 \times 2 + 2^2 \times 3 + 3^2 \times 4 + \ldots + n^2(n+1) = \dfrac{n(n+1)(n+2)(3n+1)}{12}\) for all positive integers.

label: Mathematical Induction

text: Example 5 — Type 5: MI with recursive sequences

label: Mathematical Induction
text: It is given that \(a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots, a_n, \ldots\) is a sequence of numbers, where \(a_1 = 2\) and \(a_{r+1} = 3a_r - 1\) for \(r = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\). Prove, by mathematical induction, that for all positive integers \(n\), \(a_n = \dfrac{3^n + 1}{2}\).

label: Mathematical Induction
text: Assume that \(a_m = \dfrac{3^m + 1}{2}\), where \(m\) is a positive integer.

label: Mathematical Induction

text: Exercise 24 — [Level 1]

label: Mathematical Induction
text: A sequence of numbers \(c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_n, \ldots\) is defined as \(c_1 = 2\) and \(c_{k+1} = 3c_k + 2k - 1\) for \(k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\). Using mathematical induction, prove that \(c_n = 3^n - n\) for all positive integers \(n\).

label: Mathematical Induction
text: Assume that \(c_m = 3^m - m\), where \(m\) is a positive integer.
